<reason>Side B (PRO) built its opening almost entirely against permanent summer time — an opponent Side A never defended — and Side A (CON) exploited that mismatch relentlessly and clearly: under switching, winter already runs on standard time, so every dark-bus-stop argument is satisfied by the status quo and the only live clash is summer. B's attempts to recover ("winter standard time is a concession," the biannual health spike) were partially live but never resolved the summer comparison. A also landed the sharpest single turn of the debate: using B's own criterion — light matters where people actually are — against B, since permanent standard time dumps June daylight on sleepers at 4:30 and removes it from crowded after-school and commute hours. B's answer that lost evening light is an absorbable "lifestyle tradeoff" was dismantled by A's coordination argument (bells, shifts, timetables are set by the clock), and B's decentralized-scheduling escape either fails to happen or reimports the same sleep loss in staggered, unsynchronised form. B's best asymmetry (the 1970s permanent-DST failure with no counterpart rejection of standard time) was answered plausibly: the US returned to switching, not to permanent standard time. B also pressed a fair burden on the transition harm's avoidability, and A answered it with an actual mechanism (harm proportional to acute sleep debt, autumn returns the hour, short-window event displacement) — so B's closing claim that A offered "never more than go to bed earlier" mildly misdescribes A's rebuttal. A's transient-vs-chronic weighing was the clearer decision rule. A carries execution cost for two clipped turns, which is why this stays clear rather than dominant.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's turn of B's own criterion: B conceded a 4:30 sunrise "falls on people asleep behind curtains," which A converted into the decisive point that permanent standard time wastes daylight on empty streets while stripping it from the busiest evening hours — combined with the coordination rebuttal showing B's "just shift when you go outside" fix is exactly what individuals cannot do alone.</best_rebuttal>
